items.file: Rajkumari Amrit Kaur receiving penicillin cases.jpg
items.title: Rajkumari Amrit Kaur receiving penicillin cases
items.description: Ninety-three cases of penicillin, a gift from the Canadian Red Cross to India arrived at New Delhi in a special plane from Canada on October 17, 1947. Presenting the penicillin to Rajkumari Amrit Kaur, the then Health Minister in the Government of India at the Palam aerodrome. Dr. Jivraj Mehta, Director General of Health Services appears on the left and standing on the right is Sardar Balwant Sing
items.author: Photo Division, Govt. of India

items.title: Khin Kyi with Indian women
items.description: A reception was held by Rajkumari Amrit Kaur, the then Minister for Health in the Government of India, at Government House, New Delhi on September 27, 1949 in honour of the delegates to the South East Asian Regional Conference of the WHO. Madame Aung San is seen in a group with Indian women who were present at the reception.
items.author: Photo Division, Govt. of India

items.file: Amrit Kaur, Rajagopalachari, Nehru and Khin Kyi.jpg
items.title: Amrit Kaur, Rajagopalachari, Nehru and Khin Kyi
items.description: A reception was held by Rajkumari Amrit Kaur, the then Minister for Health in the Government of India, at Government House, New Delhi on September 27, 1949 in honour of the delegates to the South East Asian Regional Conference of the WHO. From left to right are seen: Rajkumari Amrit Kaur, C. Rajagopalachari, Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru and Madame Aung San.

items.description: A reception was held by Rajkumari Amrit Kaur, the then Minister for Health in the Government of India, at Government House, New Delhi on September 27, 1949 in honour of the delegates to the South East Asian Regional Conference of the WHO. From left to right are seen: Sir Maung Gyi, Rajkumari Amrit Kaur, Madame Aung San and Dr. The Mya, Director of Public Health, Burma, at the reception.

items.file: Baby attempting to take off Maj. Gen. Thimayya's cap.jpg
items.title: Baby attempting to take off Maj. Gen. Thimayya's cap
items.description: A baby show was organized in Srinagar by the State Health Department of Jammu and Kashmir. Photograph shows the winner of the best baby award in the show making an attempt to take off (then) Major General Thimayya’s cap. Rajkumari Amrit Kaur, the then Health Minister of India is seen watching the baby.
items.author: Photo Division, Govt. of India

items.title: Bakshi Ghulam Mohd. garlanding Nehru
items.description: Bakshi Ghulam Mohammad garlands Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru on his arrival at Srinagar Airport on September 24, 1949 to participate in the All Jammu & Kashmir National Conference. Sheikh Abdullah, N. V. Gadgil, N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar and Rajkumari Amrit Kaur are also seen in the picture.
items.author: Photo Division, Govt. of India

items.title: Emblem of India
items.description: The National Emblem of India is derived from the time of the Emperor Ashoka. The emblem is a replica of the Lion of Sarnath, near Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh. The Lion Capital was erected in the third century BC by Emperor Ashoka to mark the spot where Buddha first proclaimed his gospel of peace and emancipation to the four quarters of the universe. items.author: Government of India
